WHO's latest formal Disease Outbreak News (DON615, 14 Aug) counted 4,686 confirmed cases and 2,186 deaths across all three countries as of 12 Aug — the newer ECDC/DRC figures are not yet DON-ratified.

outbreaks.name: Europe — West Nile virus (2026 season)
outbreaks.status: Seasonal transmission still accelerating; no update since last week's report
outbreaks.scope_note: Locally acquired human cases reported to ECDC for the 2026 transmission season as at 21 Aug, across 98 affected areas in 12 countries: Italy 311, Greece 157, Spain 63, North Macedonia 37, Romania 28, France 17, Serbia 6, Netherlands 2, and one each in Albania, Austria, Germany and Kosovo. ECDC's weekly human surveillance page was re-checked on 24 Aug and still shows a 21 Aug update, so these remain the current figures. ECDC does not publish a season death toll. A year earlier, 67 areas in nine countries had reported cases by this point.

outbreaks.name: Australia — H5N1 avian influenza
outbreaks.status: First infection in a local mammal; no poultry or agricultural cases reported
outbreaks.scope_note: Confirmed H5N1 detections nationwide as at Friday 21 Aug, a figure the federal government gave and CNA reported. These are animal detections, overwhelmingly in wild birds — not a human case count — and Canberra says the virus has not reached poultry or agriculture. A long-nosed fur seal found dead at Beachport, South Australia, about 310km south of Adelaide, is the country's first confirmed mammal case; the virus arrived in Australia in June and caused the country's first mass seabird deaths this month.

outbreaks.name: EU/EEA — Dermatophilus congolensis skin infections
outbreaks.status: Spreading; four new countries since the June risk assessment
outbreaks.scope_note: Confirmed human skin infections across Austria, Denmark, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and the UK, per ECDC's week-34 Communicable Disease Threats Report. Denmark, the Netherlands, Switzerland and the UK are new since ECDC's 17 Jun rapid risk assessment. Most cases are among men who have sex with men, though cases linked to martial arts and other close-contact settings are also reported. Infections have generally been mild and resolve with topical or oral antibiotics. No newer CDTR has been published — ECDC's threats feed still shows week 34 as the latest.

outbreaks.name: Europe — Salmonella Enteritidis ST11 cluster
outbreaks.status: Ongoing; 45% of cases reported since May 2026
outbreaks.scope_note: Confirmed cases reported between May 2025 and August 2026 across seven countries, per ECDC's week-34 CDTR: UK 207, Netherlands 106, Belgium 15, Germany 6, France 4, Austria 2 and Denmark 1. At least 34 have been hospitalised; ages range from 0 to 90, median 31. UK investigators suspect imported eggs while a small Dutch case-interview study points to chicken meat. No death toll is published.

outbreaks.name: Sweden & Finland — festival measles cluster
outbreaks.status: Contained so far; more cases possible among unvaccinated attendees
outbreaks.scope_note: Epidemiologically linked cases across nine regions in Sweden and one in Finland (Åland), all traced to a music festival in northern Sweden, per ECDC's week-34 CDTR. Finland reported its Åland case on 21 Aug. ECDC rates the risk to the highly vaccinated general population as low, with moderate risk for infants under 12 months and unvaccinated young children.

stories.headline: Pope Leo calls for a stronger international effort to stop Ebola in DR Congo
stories.summary: Pope Leo used his Sunday address to press for greater international support for the Bundibugyo virus response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where the outbreak is now the largest Ebola epidemic ever documented in the country.

stories.headline: Australia confirms its first H5N1 case in a local mammal
stories.summary: South Australian authorities confirmed the country's first mammalian detection of H5N1 in a long-nosed fur seal found dead with no signs of injury at Beachport, about 310km south of Adelaide. Federal Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said the death does not appear linked to other sick or dead marine mammals but warned that once H5 is spreading in the natural environment, significant losses cannot be avoided. The federal government said on Friday that 297 cases had been confirmed nationwide, none of them in poultry or agriculture.

stories.headline: ECDC's week-34 threats report tracks Ebola, West Nile, dermatophilosis, salmonella and measles
stories.summary: ECDC's Communicable Disease Threats Report for 15–21 August remains the agency's latest weekly product, covering the DR Congo Ebola epidemic, the accelerating European West Nile season, a spreading Dermatophilus congolensis cluster now in 10 countries, a seven-country Salmonella Enteritidis ST11 cluster and a Swedish–Finnish festival measles cluster.

stories.headline: WHO's latest Ebola outbreak news counts 4,686 confirmed cases as of 12 August
stories.summary: WHO's most recent Disease Outbreak News on the Bundibugyo virus epidemic, published on 14 August, recorded 4,686 confirmed cases and 2,186 deaths across the DR Congo, Uganda and one imported case in France as of 12 August, including 4,665 cases and 2,184 deaths in the DR Congo alone (case-fatality ratio 46.8 per cent). It noted 1,060 additional confirmed cases and 597 deaths since the 1 August report, partly from stronger surveillance but mostly from genuine expansion, and confirmed the outbreak has overtaken the 2018–2020 epidemic's 3,317 cases to become the largest ever documented in the country.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Patch Zimbra first: CISA put CVE-2026-73570 on its known-exploited list with a three-day federal deadline after CERT Polska saw the SNMP command-injection flaw being used from Aug 19 and Shadowserver counted more than 270 compromised servers by the weekend. Next is Keycloak, where a 9.1-rated password-reset flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker take over any account without ever touching the verification email — awkward for something that fronts single sign-on for everything else. Below the patch queue the running theme is attackers using what is already trusted, from Microsoft Defender's own signed boot driver to car head units infected through their built-in updaters. And if you run anything on AWS, the finding that more than 9,300 leaked keys are still live is worth an hour of credential rotation.

stories.headline: Microsoft's August updates break printing and PDF export in WPF apps
stories.summary: Microsoft confirmed that the August 2026 .NET Framework cumulative updates break printing and PDF export in Windows Presentation Foundation applications across Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2012 through 2025, throwing System.IO.FileFormatException errors with certain fonts such as Calibri. The temporary workaround is an AppContext switch in the application config file — but Microsoft warns it disables security protections introduced by the August updates and should only be used until a permanent fix ships.

stories.headline: Critical Keycloak password-reset flaw lets unauthenticated attackers take over any account
stories.summary: Red Hat and the Keycloak project have patched a flaw in the reset-credentials flow of the keycloak-services component, the core engine of the open-source identity and access management server. An unauthenticated remote attacker can force the password-reset process for any user without clicking the required email verification link, giving full control of the target account. Red Hat, acting as CNA, rates it 9.1 on CVSS v3.1 — a score confirmed in the NVD record. Keycloak fronts single sign-on for large numbers of internal applications, so an account takeover here can cascade; patch or upgrade first.

stories.headline: CISA orders urgent patching of actively exploited Zimbra command-injection flaw
stories.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-73570 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on Aug 21 and gave US federal civilian agencies a three-day deadline to patch. The flaw is a command injection in Zimbra Collaboration Suite's optional zimbra-snmp package: when SNMP notifications are enabled, improper sanitisation of untrusted input lets an unauthenticated attacker reach remote code execution. NVD scores it 8.9 (CVSS v3.1). CERT Polska first observed exploitation on Aug 19 and Shadowserver counted more than 270 compromised Zimbra instances by Aug 23. Versions before 10.1.20 are affected; the patch shipped on Jul 20.

stories.headline: UAT-10147 uses AI to scale server attacks, deploying SPECTRE with EDR bypass and a Linux rootkit
stories.summary: Researchers detailed a Chinese-speaking cybercrime group tracked as UAT-10147 that is targeting Windows and Linux web servers worldwide across the education, media, technology and gaming sectors, with most victims in Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada and Vietnam. The group deploys a toolkit dubbed SPECTRE that pairs EDR bypass with a Linux rootkit, and uses AI tooling to scale its attacks. Details emerged after researchers found an exposed attacker-controlled server.

stories.headline: Operation QUICSILVER targets Myanmar government and IT sectors with the QUICAgent backdoor
stories.summary: Seqrite Labs flagged an espionage campaign it calls Operation QUICSILVER, which uses graduation ceremony invitation lures to deliver a Go-based backdoor named QUICAgent against government and IT targets in Myanmar. The activity is assessed with moderate confidence to be the work of a China-nexus threat actor.

stories.headline: ToxicPanda 2.0 abuses Android VPN permissions to cut phones off from Google Play
stories.summary: Zimperium reported a new version of the ToxicPanda banking trojan that targets 349 financial and cryptocurrency apps across 16 countries, stealing credentials through invisible overlays and a spoofed lock screen. Its notable new trick is abusing Android's VPN service permission to stand up a local network interface that blocks communication with Google Play, cutting off Play Protect verification and security updates. The malware now supports 167 remote commands and abuses Android's Wireless Debugging Bridge for shell-level device access, and is distributed via AWS-hosted buckets.

stories.headline: Malware infects Android car head units through their own built-in updaters
stories.summary: Kaspersky, which found the threat in June 2026, described a malware family built specifically to infect Android-based vehicle head-unit firmware made by DoFun. It spreads through the units' own built-in updaters and delivers a multi-stage downloader whose end goals are ad fraud and enrolling the head units into a proxy botnet.

stories.headline: TikTok agrees to US$400 million settlement in US child privacy lawsuit
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice said ByteDance-owned TikTok will pay US$400 million to settle a 2024 lawsuit alleging violations of US child privacy law. TikTok pays US$300 million immediately and a further US$100 million on entry of an order vacating a prior consent decree against the company.

stories.headline: 14 trojanised npm packages drop the RedC2 4.0 Linux backdoor
stories.summary: TrendAI, Trend Micro's research arm, found a set of trojanised npm packages posing as working calendar and streak utilities that quietly deliver an AI-assisted Linux implant called RedC2 4.0. When the module loads it locates a bundled binary, marks it executable and launches it as a detached background process. Check your lockfiles and CI images if you pull small utility packages unpinned.

stories.headline: New SynkLoader malware pushed through Microsoft Teams help-desk phishing
stories.summary: Researchers at Expel identified a previously unknown malware family, SynkLoader, combining Python, PowerShell, C# and C++ and deploying modules for credential theft, remote access and persistence. Attackers impersonate a company IT help desk over Microsoft Teams and steer victims to download a fake "PowerShell Cleaner" MSI hosted on Microsoft Azure so it looks legitimate. Expel first saw it around Jul 28 and, based on its Active Directory profiling, assesses it is built to set up ransomware in enterprise networks.

stories.headline: Thousands of leaked AWS keys are still live, hundreds with full account control
stories.summary: Truffle Security, which tracked publicly exposed AWS credentials over four years, found 64,024 unique keys across 50,654 accounts, of which 10,616 were still functional when tested (88 per cent authenticating as of Aug 10). More than 9,300 remain active, and 817 belong to companies — 526 of those root keys and 242 carrying full AdministratorAccess. Hugging Face was the single largest source at 8,482 unique key exposures. A valid key of this kind gives an attacker full control of the account: data theft, infrastructure takeover, cryptomining or deletion.

stories.headline: Microsoft Defender's own boot-time driver can be turned against security software
stories.summary: Check Point Research disclosed a technique that abuses BTR.sys, Microsoft Defender's legitimately signed Boot Time Removal Tool driver, to perform arbitrary kernel-level file and registry operations on Windows 7 through Windows 11 25H2. No software flaw is exploited and no external driver is imported — the attacker uses a component already present and trusted on the machine, which is what makes it awkward to block. It can be used to delete other security software at boot.
